scenes.headline: Liquid Clustering
scenes.subtitle: Adaptive data layout without partitioning
scenes.narration: Liquid clustering is a flexible Delta layout that clusters data by chosen keys without rigid physical partitioning.

scenes.headline: What liquid clustering solves
items: Avoids the small-files and skew problems of partitions
Lets you change clustering keys without rewriting layout
scenes.narration: Liquid clustering unifies what partitioning and Z-order did separately. It sidesteps the tiny-file explosion and skew that bad partition keys cause. Crucially, you can evolve the clustering keys later without a full table rewrite.

scenes.headline: Enabling liquid clustering
scenes.narration: The CLUSTER BY clause sets the columns Delta uses to co-locate data. Unlike partitioning, you can alter those keys later without rewriting existing files. Running OPTIMIZE incrementally clusters newly written data into the layout.

scenes.headline: Partitioning + Z-order vs liquid clustering

columns.title: Partition + Z-order
points: Prone to skew and small files

scenes.narration: Traditional partitioning locks you into columns that are painful to change and easy to get wrong. Liquid clustering lets keys evolve as query patterns shift, with no costly rewrite. It also clusters incrementally and avoids the classic partition pitfalls.

scenes.headline: When to use it
items: New tables where query patterns may evolve
High-cardinality keys that partitioning handles poorly
Workloads needing both good writes and reads
scenes.narration: Reach for liquid clustering on new tables whose access patterns are uncertain. It handles high-cardinality keys that would wreck a partition scheme. It also balances read performance with efficient, low-overhead writes.

scenes.text: Liquid clustering gives Z-order-like skipping with the flexibility partitions never had.
scenes.narration: Set your cluster keys, and change them freely as your queries evolve.
